product.name: Connectors
product.lede: Connectors lets applications and agents discover and use integrations through typed, versioned contracts. Each adapter owns its provider's behaviour; a catalog provider serves ordinary HTTP APIs straight from their pinned OpenAPI documents. Credentials stay in custody, writes need an approval, and an uncertain outcome is never sent twice.
product.meta: Rust services, a local CLI and shared contracts · Linux x86_64 source release · MIT OR Apache-2.0

sections.title: One boundary between an application and every provider it calls.
sections.lede: A caller learns what an adapter offers from its descriptor and invokes it the same way everywhere. What a provider means stays with that provider's adapter.

items.title: Contracts describe guarantees
items.description: Inputs, outputs, access, lifecycle, partial results and failures are part of a versioned contract, not of one provider's habits.

items.title: Adapters own their provider
items.description: Kubernetes selectors, PostgreSQL query rules and Loki's LogQL stay in their adapter. Shared contracts never import a provider.

items.title: HTTP APIs without adapter code
items.description: The catalog provider binds operations from a pinned OpenAPI document: GitLab, Jira, Confluence, HubSpot, Zendesk, Google and Runpod.

items.title: Credentials in custody
items.description: A saved connection keeps its credential in the Secret Service keyring. It never travels in operation input or through a federation gateway.

items.title: Writes under approval
items.description: A write is admitted against a policy and a protected proof bound to its whole input, and a guard declared as data can check the provider before and after.

items.title: Uncertain is not failed
items.description: A write whose answer is lost is outcome_unknown with its recorded attempt. Nothing resends it.

steps.title: Describe
steps.description: The client reads the adapter's descriptor: operations, schemas, contract and profile, and a revision.

steps.title: Select access
steps.description: A connection binds a chosen target and credential. Discovering an endpoint grants nothing.

steps.title: Invoke
steps.description: The request names the operation and the descriptor revision it was built against. The host admits it or refuses it before dispatch.

steps.title: Interpret
steps.description: The result carries provenance and completeness, or a typed refusal, or an explicitly unknown outcome.

sections.title: What runs, and the test that holds it.
sections.lede: Shipped means it runs on main and a named test holds it. Decided means specified with no runtime. Planned means not built.

tools.name: Entity Runtime
tools.description: Deterministic decisions over recorded state. The local CLI keeps connection metadata, approvals and audit as Entity Runtime records.

tools.name: Eventlog
tools.description: Append-only event storage. Entity Runtime keeps the local metadata store on its SQLite provider.
